title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.8978: the fused arrival with a 2^25-row table, checkpoint period 2048 and h = 0.000065

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.8978 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on kaankolcu's cbea87bf (125.8982: bradcush's 4c8222cc with each walk's arrival fused into pass 1, kernels/secp_fuse.s), whose kernels, prices and rows it keeps except the two arrival BFI widths, with three changes: a partition table of R = 2^25 rows (both BFIs write 26 bits; doubling rate 1/(6R) + 2^-47.99999 <= 2^-27.5849 per step); the checkpoint period raised from 256 to 2048 (anchor work 14*ceil((S_int + 2^61)/2048) milli-units); and the Markov headroom h = 0.000065 with p0 = 0.3900653. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census under the rule of 5f1ae3ce, now with a new 64-table run at R = 2^25: (1 + w)(kappa_eff + 2 s.e.) is 1.00002 for the main run and 1.000079 for the pool of the ten walk runs; two period-2048 controls match their period-256 runs. The ordinary step is 129.03125 + 444.515625 + 25614/2^20 = 573.5713 instructions; the declared run executes the fused pass 1, the loops and the arrival rows at exactly these counts and enters all 1,167 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.010e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995433, phase 1 = 2^125.897588, hard extras = 2^109.957111, random extras = 2^98.7873, allowance = 2^112.6965, W_ledger = 2^125.8977642 < 2^125.8978; Markov ratio 0.0000526750 < 0.000065; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1258978 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1258977 exactly. No prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (entering every rare-exit stub), the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, big integers, a bit-exact address model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions.
